tickets.title: Security
tickets.description: Protect student schedules and academic information from unauthorized access. Ensure that students can only view their own academic data.

tickets.title: Auditability
tickets.description: Record all prerequisite override actions with advisor identity, timestamp, and justification to support auditing and compliance requirements.

tickets.title: Usability
tickets.description: Provide an intuitive drag-and-drop academic planning experience that allows students to create and manage roadmaps with minimal training.

tickets.title: Build Academic Roadmap
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to add courses to my academic roadmap, so that I can plan my degree progression and graduate on time.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Student can search and select a course from the catalog.
- Student can add the course to an academic roadmap.
- Added courses are displayed immediately in the roadmap.
- The roadmap is saved successfully.
- PASS: The selected course appears in the roadmap after saving.
- FAIL: The course is not displayed or cannot be saved.

tickets.title: Drag and Drop Schedule Planning
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to drag and drop courses into a calendar, so that I can visualize my semester schedule before registration.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Student can drag a course from the course catalog.
- Student can drop the course into a calendar slot.
- The calendar updates immediately after the course is dropped.
- The schedule remains visible after saving.
- PASS: The course appears in the selected calendar slot.
- FAIL: The course is not displayed correctly.

tickets.title: Prerequisite Validation
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want the system to automatically validate course prerequisites, so that I do not accidentally select courses I am not eligible to take.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The system checks prerequisite requirements when a student adds a course.
- A warning message is displayed if prerequisites are not satisfied.
- Students can view which prerequisite is missing.
- Courses with unmet prerequisites cannot be added unless an advisor override exists.
- PASS: The system correctly identifies miss

tickets.title: Morning Class Warning
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to receive a warning when selecting classes that start at 8:00 AM, so that I can make better scheduling decisions.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The system identifies classes that start at 8:00 AM.
- A warning message is displayed before the class is added.
- Students may continue or cancel the selection.
- The warning does not prevent enrollment if the student confirms.
- PASS: The warning appears whenever an 8:00 AM class is selected.
- FAIL: No warning is displayed.

tickets.title: Manual Prerequisite Override
tickets.description:
As an Advisor, I want to manually override prerequisite requirements, so that students with approved exceptions can enroll in courses.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Advisors can access the prerequisite override function.
- The advisor must provide a justification before confirming the override.
- The override action is recorded in the audit log.
- The affected student can subsequently add the course.

analysis.ambiguity1:
Requirement: "I want the app to warn me if I'm choosing a class that starts at 8:00 AM."

Why it is vague:
It lacks clear system boundaries and specific metrics. It does not define what the warning entails—whether it is a hard system block preventing enrollment, or a dismissible visual alert that the user can bypass.
analysis.ambiguity2:
Requirement: "I want to be able to override the system manually if a student has special permission."

Why it is vague:
The term "special permission" is undefined. It does not specify the criteria for this permission, who has the authority to grant it, or how the system logically verifies this status before allowing the override.
analysis.conflictSolution:
Conflict:
The Registrar requires that students cannot add full classes to their roadmap, while the Head of Advising wants students to plan their academic path several years in advance, even when future class availability is unknown.

Proposed Solution:
The system should support two planning modes. In Long-Term Planning Mode, students may add future courses regardless of current seat availability. In Registration Mode, the system must validate real-time enrollment data and prevent registration for classes that are already full. This allows strategic degree planning while maintaining accurate enrollment controls.
analysis.nfr1: Security - Student data is sensitive; the system must ensure under no circumstances can a student view another student's schedule.
analysis.nfr2: Usability - The system must provide an intuitive drag-and-drop calendar interface to solve the issue of the \"ugly\" course catalog.
analysis.nfr3: Auditability - The system must securely log every instance an advisor manually overrides a prerequisite for audit purposes.
